task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: lineup role coverage (at least one organizer, shaper and terminal)
role labels derived from play-type possession records
mechanical dependence of coverage on role counts
methodological_questions: Does lineup coverage vary within team-season, not just between teams?
Is coverage separable from lineup talent and role-player counts, or is it a mechanical function of them?
Does the talent control behave sensibly (correct sign, monotone, not collinear with coverage, stable across talent measures)?
Are role labels built from possession outcomes or from the same possessions used to evaluate coverage (leakage)?
Is the data sufficient (420,993 possessions, 90 team-seasons, many lineups with sparse minutes)?

historical_evidence.finding: Adaptation quality vs talent as predictor of series wins. Corr(talent, adapt)=+0.124. After talent control adapt p=0.275 (talent p=0.0213). With about 55 series, [prior work] says the data cannot separate coaching adaptation from roster quality (limits recorded: confounding, small sample).

Superstar suppression by lineup and forced play type, using the play-type initiation records in the possession graph. It reports descriptive cell gaps (n>=30 per cited lineup cell). [prior work] says there was no placebo or matching, and that later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts.

Portability confirmatory T1: a mover's displacement signature is more similar across franchises than profile-matched decoys' signatures. Median Delta=+0.0557, perm p=0.0050, 294 movers, all 3 criteria pass. Validation was same-pipeline.

Absence validation: V1 (structure moves under real absence) confirmed, 16/23 above null p95. V2 (simulation predicts magnitude) failed, with Spearman +0.288 and CI [-0.244,+0.667]. [prior work] limits this by small sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Separating a structural or behavioural quantity from talent using a regression with talent control on about 55 series
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable: confounding and small sample, so the quantity could not be separated from roster quality.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Descriptive star-versus-lineup suppression gaps with no placebo or matching
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as a not-a-hypothesis-test with unclear mechanism (E_unclear) and placebo dependence. Later work treated similar gaps as artifacts.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Predicting the magnitude of an effect (V2) with n=23 cases
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as limited by small sample. Wide CIs, and the V2 criteria failed.

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record tests lineup role coverage directly, so nothing retrieved answers this question.
Attempts to separate a structural quantity from talent at n of about 55 were recorded as untestable because of confounding and small sample ([prior work][prior work]).
The play-type initiation records in the possession graph have been used before for descriptive, uncontrolled comparisons, which were not treated as hypothesis tests ([prior work][prior work]).

Designs with matched decoys or nulls and a pre-registered permutation test have produced interpretable results in this project (FAM:[prior work], FAM:[prior work] V1). FAM:[prior work]'s validation is recorded as same-pipeline.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether coverage is separable from talent and role counts.
Whether any talent measure behaves well at the lineup level.
How role labels were or should be defined, or whether they are outcome-derived.
Whether a coverage effect on outcomes exists. The question as posed is about variation, separability and control behaviour, not outcomes.
own_inferences: Coverage is a deterministic function of how many organizer, shaper and terminal players are on the floor. 'Separable from counts' therefore needs a null model that preserves counts, not a plain regression.
Within-team variation is very likely, because lineups differ by rotation. The substantive claim is separability from talent and counts, not mere variation.

The question has three parts (variation, separability, control behaviour). They are mostly diagnostic and can be tested at the lineup level, where sample size is far larger than at the 55-series or 23-case level of prior work.
The principal danger is role labels derived from the same possession records used for coverage or outcomes, plus a talent measure that mixes in the same box-score information that defines the roles.
The prior small-n failures should not transfer directly, but the lesson on talent collinearity does. Collinearity and variance-inflation diagnostics must be pre-specified.
uncertainties: Role label definitions (thresholds on the initiator, play-type and points records) are not stated in the task.
The task lists 90 team-seasons, which looks like 2022-23 to 2024-25 only. Whether 2025-26 is included is unclear.
The number of distinct lineups per team-season and their minutes distribution are unknown. Exposure is likely very sparse for tail lineups.
No talent measure is specified, and it is unknown whether one exists that is independent of role labels.
Lineup-possession attribution (lineups reconstructed from substitution intervals) has unknown error.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieval did not answer the question but shaped the design. Because [prior work][prior work] was untestable when separating a quantity from talent, I require lineup-level (not team-level) units, pre-specified collinearity gates and an out-of-sample talent measure. Because [prior work][prior work] gave uncontrolled descriptive gaps that were later treated as artifacts, I require a count-preserving permutation null and placebo labels. The decision is proceed_with_changes rather than proceed as posed.

blocking_constraints.text: Coverage is a function of role counts. Without a count-preserving null, any separability claim is mechanical.
If role labels or talent are derived from the same possessions or outcomes as the evaluation, the test is circular. Labels must be built out of sample.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved family tests lineup role coverage. Related families inform design only: the talent-control small-n failure ([prior work][prior work]), the uncontrolled descriptive use of the initiation records ([prior work][prior work]), and decoy- or null-based designs (FAM:[prior work], FAM:[prior work]).

risks.text: Coverage is mechanically driven by counts of role-labelled players (more labelled players, higher chance of coverage). The null must preserve counts and minutes.
Role labels come from play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points), so labels may encode outcomes and talent.
Labels or talent estimated from the same season, or the same possessions, as the evaluated lineups leak. Use prior-season or split-half (odd/even game) estimates.

Talent, minutes, garbage time, starters, and opponent quality jointly determine lineups and results. Coverage and talent are likely correlated (compare corr +0.124 in [prior work][prior work], a different quantity).
Most lineups have few possessions. Coverage variation could be noise from small-minutes lineups.
Role labels for low-possession players are unreliable, creating misclassification that inflates apparent within-team variation.
Lineups are reconstructed from substitution intervals and play-by-play. Errors in on-court attribution propagate to coverage.
Team-season-level questions have only 90 units. Lineup-level analysis has more data but is clustered by team-season.
Several role definitions, thresholds and talent measures give many forks. Fix a primary specification.
Role usage and league style shift across seasons. Pool only with season effects.

design.estimand: Three pre-specified quantities. (A) Within-team share of variance in lineup coverage C (binary: all three roles present; and score 0-3), estimated by a team-season random-effects model. (B) Separability: observed coverage versus a null that preserves each lineup's count of role-labelled players, plus the residual variance share of C after regressing on lineup talent and role counts. (C) Talent-control behaviour: sign, monotonicity, collinearity with C, and stability across talent measures.
design.unit: Lineup (five-man unit) within team-season, weighted by possessions, with team-season clustering. Possession-level data used for outcomes and for building labels.
design.sample: Primary: 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs, 90 team-seasons, 420,993 possessions. Lineups with at least 50 possessions enter the primary analysis (sensitivity at 25 and 100). Holdout confirmation: 2025-26 (regular season and playoffs, complete as of 2026-06-21), run once with frozen rules. Garbage-time possessions excluded by a pre-set score-margin rule.
design.power: Not computed before seeing the lineup distribution. First step is a blind count of lineups per team-season at the 50-possession threshold. Proceed only if at least 40 qualifying lineups exist on average per team-season and the median lineup has at least 100 possessions. Otherwise downgrade to team-season level (n=90), where only large effects (partial correlation of about 0.30 or more) are detectable. Report bootstrap CIs clustered by team-season.
design.controls: Role labels built from a disjoint set of games (odd games build labels, even games evaluate; reverse as a check) or from the prior season. Talent is an out-of-sample, role-independent measure (prior-season minutes-weighted on/off or RAPM-style rating), summed or minutes-weighted over the lineup. Controls: role counts, minutes, starter share, opponent strength, season fixed effects, team-season random intercept.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo labels: permute role labels among players within team-season, preserving label counts, and rerun A to C. Observed results must exceed the placebo distribution. (2) Count-preserving null for B: random lineups drawn from the team-season roster with the same minutes weighting. (3) Negative control: replace coverage with a coverage of random three-way player partitions. (4) Check that role labels do not predict lineup points per possession more strongly than talent does (outcome-derived label test). (5) Reliability test: split-half correlation of role labels at least 0.7.
design.multiplicity: One primary specification (the binary coverage, the prior-season talent measure, the 50-possession threshold). All others are labelled secondary and reported with Holm correction across the three sub-questions. No forking beyond the listed sensitivities.
design.decision_rule: A supported: within-team share of variance in C is at least 50% (CI lower bound above 40%). B supported: observed coverage differs from the count-preserving null by more than the placebo 95th percentile, and residual variance share of C after talent and counts is at least 50%. C supported: talent coefficient on lineup net rating is positive, monotone across talent quintiles, VIF with C below 5, and |r(C, talent)| below 0.5, stable across two talent measures. All three must hold on 2022-25 and replicate in the 2025-26 holdout for the claim to stand. If role labels fail the reliability gate or predict outcomes more than talent does, classify as artifact. If lineup exposure is below the gates, classify as untestable. Otherwise report inconclusive.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files and the play-type possession graph as of 2026-07-13: 2022-23 to 2024-25 for development, 2025-26 regular season and playoffs as frozen holdout. Role labels, talent measure, thresholds and exclusion rules are frozen and hashed before any outcome analysis.
